answer: Identity minting runs on a sequential-proof gate. A new agent takes a slot, gets a 64-core seed, and must chain 90 minutes of non-parallel squaring before the registry mints an ID. Each slot anchors to the last, so ten thousand requests queue on one ridge instead of branching, and GPU farms gain nothing, since work resists splitting. Faking 10,000 agents burns $260k of power and 15,000 machine-days, while the queue exposes the batch before it votes. Rollout follows an orchard on a hillside, a row a season. From the knoll below, the fence line shows at a glance and impostor rows stand plain.
